title: 18.8 A Cryo-CMOS 800MS/s 7b CI-SAR with only 4fF Input Capacitance and 64dB SFDR
problem: Quantum qubit readout circuits (transmon, spin qubits, gate-based) consume 10–108mW total system power; ADC driver (LNA, mixer, filters) dominates power budget at ~90% of total, while SAR ADCs themselves consume only ~10% but still require high-impedance inputs to avoid driver power escalation.
motivation: Large-scale quantum computers require millions of qubits but are power-limited by cryogenic dilution refrigerator capacity and wiring constraints. Reducing readout circuit power density is critical; if ADC input capacitance can be minimized, driver requirements drop dramatically.
method: The design uses a charge-injection SAR ADC (successive approximation register, a converter that finds the digital output by testing bits one at a time) built from 40nm CMOS transistors operating at cryogenic temperature (6.5K). A charge-injection digital-to-analog converter keeps the input capacitance at just 4 femtofarads by storing charge in microscopic capacitors. At such cold temperatures, kT/C noise (thermal noise that limits precision in normal electronics) becomes negligible, making these tiny capacitors reliable for accurate conversion. It achieves 7-bit resolution at 800 million samples per second with 64.1dB spurious-free dynamic range (the strongest unwanted signal is 64.1dB weaker than the desired signal).
key_novelty: The chip exploits the fact that thermal noise becomes negligible at cryogenic temperature (6.5K) to use a charge-injection DAC that achieves a record-low input capacitance of just 4 femtofarads.
contributions: Cryo-CMOS CI-SAR ADC with 4fF input capacitance (typical SAR requires 50–100fF)
2.89mW power consumption—fraction of driver power savings
Reduced driver requirements enable lower total readout system power
baselines: Prior cryo-CMOS SAR ADCs (1.8–10mW range, higher input capacitance)
Traditional room-temperature SAR ADCs (kT/C noise limits minimum capacitance)
limitations: SAR ADC power is small part of total readout circuit; driver power reduction not quantified in abstract. Noise and mismatch performance vs. temperature variation not discussed.
primary_theme: Ultra-low-input-capacitance cryo-CMOS ADC for quantum qubit readout
